about: Galaxy Digital is a New York-based financial services and digital assets firm founded by Mike Novogratz in 2018, offering trading, asset management, investment banking, staking and Bitcoin mining and data centre infrastructure, including AI and high-performance computing hosting in Texas. Clients are institutions and crypto-native businesses; revenue comes from trading, fees and mining. It completed a US listing on Nasdaq (GLXY) in 2025. Business-to-business brand known in crypto circles with limited mainstream consumer awareness.

ICICI Bank is one of India's largest private sector banks, headquartered in Mumbai (registered in Vadodara), serving retail, SME and corporate customers through roughly 6,500 branches and over 16,000 ATMs, plus mobile apps such as iMobile Pay. It has international branches and subsidiaries in the UK, Canada and Singapore. It also owns ICICI Prudential insurance and mutual fund joint ventures. Founded 1994, listed on NSE, BSE and NYSE (IBN). Very strong consumer brand across India and an existing sports sponsor.

Industrial Bank Co., Ltd. is a Chinese national joint-stock commercial bank headquartered in Fuzhou, Fujian, listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange. Founded 1988, it is a significant mid-sized lender with corporate, retail, green finance and financial markets businesses and hundreds of branches across China. Provincial government and state-linked entities are among shareholders. Revenue comes from loan interest and fees. Strong domestic reputation in green finance, though little recognition outside China.

ING Group is a Dutch banking and financial services group headquartered in Amsterdam and listed on Euronext Amsterdam and the NYSE (INGA). It serves around 40 million customers across more than 100 countries with retail and direct banking, notably in the Netherlands, Belgium, Germany, Poland and Australia, plus wholesale banking for corporates. Revenue comes from lending margins and fees, with roughly 60,000 employees. Strong consumer brand in Europe with long track record in sport and cultural sponsorship.

Intesa Sanpaolo is Italy's largest banking group, headquartered in Turin with offices in Milan, formed in 2007 through the merger of Banca Intesa and Sanpaolo IMI. It serves around 13 million customers in Italy through retail, private, corporate and wealth management, with banking subsidiaries across Central and Eastern Europe and Egypt. Listed on Borsa Italiana (ISP) and employing over 90,000 people. Strong Italian consumer brand with extensive sponsorship in arts and sport.

Islamic Development Bank (IsDB) is a multilateral development financing institution headquartered in Jeddah, Saudi Arabia, established in 1973 and owned by around 57 member countries. It finances infrastructure, trade, education and health projects in Muslim-majority countries through Sharia-compliant instruments, with an AAA credit rating and subscribed capital in the tens of billions of dollars. Customers are governments, public agencies and private sector projects. Not a consumer brand; sponsorship interest would be institutional and reputational.

Japan Bank for International Cooperation (JBIC) is a Japanese government-owned policy financial institution headquartered in Tokyo, wholly owned by the Government of Japan. It provides export credits, overseas investment loans and project finance to support Japanese companies abroad and strategic resource security, working with commercial banks on infrastructure, energy and manufacturing projects worldwide. Funded by government sources and bonds. Public sector institution, not a consumer brand.

Macquarie Group is an Australian global financial services group headquartered in Sydney and listed on the ASX (MQG), operating in about 30 markets with roughly 20,000 employees. Businesses cover asset management (Macquarie Asset Management), banking and financial services, commodities and global markets, and Macquarie Capital advisory. It owns and invests in infrastructure and renewable assets, with annual income around 17 billion Australian dollars. Founded 1969. Strong corporate brand, with sponsorship history in Australian sport and events.

Mizuho Financial Group is one of Japan's three megabanks, headquartered in Tokyo (Otemachi) and listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange and NYSE (MFG). It operates Mizuho Bank, Mizuho Trust and Mizuho Securities, serving individuals, corporations and institutions in Japan and around 35 countries with roughly 60,000 employees. Revenue comes from lending, securities and asset management. Formed in 2000 from the merger of Dai-Ichi Kangyo, Fuji and Industrial Bank of Japan. Strong Japanese consumer brand with sport and cultural sponsorships.

National Australia Bank (NAB) is one of Australia's big four banks, headquartered in Melbourne and listed on the ASX (NAB). It serves around 10 million customers with personal, business and corporate banking, wealth management and institutional banking in Australia and New Zealand (BNZ), and has a large business banking franchise. Founded 1858 with about 38,000 employees. Strong consumer brand in Australia and an existing sports and cultural sponsor, including the AFL.

National Bank for Financing Infrastructure and Development (NaBFID) is an Indian government-owned development financial institution headquartered in Mumbai, set up by an Act of Parliament in 2021 to fund long-term infrastructure projects such as roads, power, ports and railways. It lends to project developers and issues bonds, with equity from the Government of India. Operating since 2021. Public sector financier with no consumer brand profile.

about: NatWest Markets is the investment banking arm of NatWest Group, based in London, providing rates, currencies, financing and debt capital markets services to corporate, institutional and public sector clients in the UK and Europe. It was restructured after the 2008 financial crisis to be smaller and ring-fenced from retail banking, as part of the UK government-linked NatWest Group, which is listed on the LSE (NWG). B2B markets business; parent NatWest is a major consumer brand and sports sponsor.

NIIF Infrastructure Finance Limited (NIIF IFL) is an Indian infrastructure financing non-bank financial company based in Mumbai, sponsored by the National Investment and Infrastructure Fund, which is backed by the Government of India and global investors. It provides long-term loans and debt to roads, renewable energy, ports and urban infrastructure projects. Customers are infrastructure developers and project companies. Formerly IDFC Infrastructure Finance. B2B financial company with no consumer profile.
cb_desc: NIIF IFL provides infrastructure debt fund and long term...

about: OCBC Bank (Oversea-Chinese Banking Corporation) is the second-largest bank in Southeast Asia by assets, headquartered in Singapore and listed on the Singapore Exchange (O39). It provides consumer, SME and corporate banking, wealth management through Bank of Singapore, and insurance via Great Eastern, with a network across Singapore, Malaysia, Indonesia, Greater China and others. Founded 1932 through a merger of three banks. Strong consumer brand in Singapore with a long history of sports and community sponsorship, including cycling and golf.

Ping An Bank is a Chinese national joint-stock commercial bank headquartered in Shenzhen, majority-owned by the Ping An Insurance group and listed on the Shenzhen Stock Exchange (000001). It offers retail banking, credit cards, wealth management, SME and corporate banking through hundreds of branches, with a strong fintech and cross-selling focus within the Ping An ecosystem. Revenue comes from loan interest and fees. Its parent is a household name in China, with extensive sports sponsorship, including football.

Power Finance Corporation (PFC) is an Indian government-owned non-banking finance company headquartered in New Delhi, listed on the NSE and BSE. It provides loans and financing to state utilities, generation companies and renewable power projects, and also owns REC Limited. Loan assets run into the trillions of rupees. Founded 1986 and owned majority by the Government of India. B2B financier with low consumer profile.

Qatar Islamic Bank (QIB) is Qatar's largest Islamic bank, headquartered in Doha and listed on the Qatar Stock Exchange (QIBK). It offers Sharia-compliant retail, corporate and wealth banking, with subsidiaries and affiliates abroad. Founded 1982, with the Qatari state and royals among shareholders. Strong national consumer brand and sponsor of sports and cultural events in Qatar.

Riyad Bank is one of Saudi Arabia's largest banks, headquartered in Riyadh and listed on the Saudi Exchange (Tadawul). Founded 1957, it provides retail, corporate, treasury, Islamic and private banking through a network of branches and ATMs across the Kingdom, with international arms in London, Houston and Singapore and a stake in Riyad Capital. The Public Investment Fund and GOSI-linked institutions are major shareholders. Strong Saudi consumer brand and an active sponsor of football and sports events.

Saudi National Bank (SNB), headquartered in Jeddah, is Saudi Arabia's largest bank by assets, created in 2021 by the merger of National Commercial Bank (NCB) and Samba Financial Group. It provides retail, corporate, treasury, wealth and Sharia-compliant banking, with branches in Saudi Arabia and offshore operations. The Public Investment Fund holds around 37 percent. Listed on the Saudi Exchange. Strong consumer brand in the Kingdom, including football and event sponsorships such as the Saudi Pro League.

Sharjah Islamic Bank is a Sharjah-based bank in the United Arab Emirates, offering Sharia-compliant retail, corporate and SME banking, finance and investment products through branches in the emirate and the wider UAE. Government of Sharjah entities are major shareholders; it is listed on the Abu Dhabi Securities Exchange and grew from the former National Bank of Sharjah. Revenue is financing profit and fees. Regional bank with moderate consumer recognition in the UAE.
cb_desc: Sharjah Islamic Bank's reputation and continued...

about: Starwood Property Trust is a large US commercial real estate finance company and mortgage REIT, headquartered in Greenwich, Connecticut with operations from San Francisco, listed on the NYSE (STWD). It originates and invests in commercial mortgage loans, infrastructure lending and property investments. Managed by affiliates of Starwood Capital Group and Barry Sternlicht. Founded 2009. Customers are property owners and developers; B2B financier with low consumer profile.

Sumitomo Mitsui Financial Group (SMFG) is one of Japan's three megabanks, headquartered in Tokyo and listed on the Tokyo Stock Exchange and NYSE (SMFG). It runs Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation, SMBC Nikko Securities, SMBC Consumer Finance and Sumitomo Mitsui Card, with large operations in Asia and stakes in Jefferies and Indian lender Yes Bank. Employs more than 100,000 people. Founded 2002. Strong Japanese consumer brand and a major sponsor in sport and culture, including golf and tennis.

Toronto-Dominion Bank (TD Bank Group) is one of Canada's Big Five banks, headquartered in Toronto, with large US operations as TD Bank, America's Most Convenient Bank. It offers retail, commercial, wealth, insurance and capital markets services to over 27 million customers, and is listed on the TSX and NYSE (TD). Assets exceed 2 trillion Canadian dollars and it has about 100,000 employees. Founded 1955. Strong consumer brand across Canada and the US east coast, with large sponsorships including TD Garden.

United Overseas Bank (UOB) is one of the three Singapore banking groups, headquartered in Singapore and listed on the Singapore Exchange (U11). It provides personal, SME, corporate, wealth and private banking across Southeast Asia (Singapore, Malaysia, Thailand, Indonesia, Vietnam) and Greater China, with over 500 branches. Founded 1935. Employs about 28,000 people, with annual income around 14 billion Singapore dollars. Strong consumer brand in Southeast Asia, a major arts and sports sponsor in Singapore.

United Wholesale Mortgage (UWM) is the largest US wholesale mortgage lender, based in Pontiac, Michigan and listed on the NYSE (UWMC). It originates home loans only through independent mortgage brokers, not directly to consumers, funding well over 100 billion dollars of loans yearly, and it has barred brokers who also work with rival Rocket Mortgage. Founded 1986, controlled by CEO Mat Ishbia, who also owns the NBA Phoenix Suns. B2B mortgage brand, with some consumer visibility through sports sponsorships.

Yes Bank is an Indian private sector bank headquartered in Mumbai, founded 2004 and listed on NSE and BSE. After a 2020 collapse and RBI-led rescue involving SBI, ICICI and others, it was restructured and in 2025 Japan's Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation took a large stake of about 20 percent. It offers retail, SME and corporate banking, digital payments and trade finance across India with over 1,000 branches. Recognisable Indian consumer brand and an existing sponsor of cricket and tennis events.

Ant Group is the Chinese fintech giant behind Alipay, headquartered in Hangzhou and affiliated with Alibaba founder Jack Ma. It operates a payments app used by over a billion people, plus wealth management (Fund Sales), credit (Huabei, Jiebei), insurance, MYbank and international payments such as Alipay+ and Ant International. Revenue is over 100 billion yuan. Spun from Alibaba in 2014; its 2020 IPO was halted by regulators. Privately held. Very strong consumer brand in China and widely used by Chinese tourists abroad.

BILL (formerly Bill.com) is a US financial automation software company headquartered in San Jose, California and listed on the NYSE (BILL). It provides accounts payable, receivable and spend management tools, including Divvy corporate cards and Invoice2go, to over 400,000 small and mid-sized businesses and accounting firms, with revenue near 1.4 billion dollars. Founded 2006. Customers pay subscription, interchange and transaction fees. B2B brand well known among US accountants and small businesses.

Freedom Mortgage is a large US mortgage lender and servicer, family-owned and based in the Boca Raton/Mount Laurel area, originating FHA, VA and conventional home loans and servicing a portfolio worth hundreds of billions of dollars. Founded 1990 by Stan Middleman. It is among the larger US non-bank lenders. Customers are home buyers and refinancers. Consumer mortgage brand with moderate US awareness. (Limited public information - check before outreach.)

about: Regional Management Corp. is a US consumer finance company headquartered in Greer, South Carolina and listed on the NYSE (RM). It makes small instalment loans, auto-secured loans and credit cards to customers with limited access to bank credit through over 350 branches in about 20 states and online, with a loan portfolio near 2 billion dollars. Founded 1987. Revenue is interest and fees. Regional consumer lender with limited national awareness.

Sabadell Consumer Finance is the consumer lending arm of Spain's Banco Sabadell, based in Sabadell, Catalonia, providing point-of-sale finance, personal loans and credit cards for retail, car and household purchases through partners and branches. Customers are Spanish consumers and retail partners. It is owned by Banco Sabadell, which is listed on the Spanish stock exchange and fended off a takeover bid from BBVA in 2025. B2B2C financier with low brand awareness of its own.
cb_desc: Sabadell Consumer Finance is a company specializing in...

about: KfW is Germany's state-owned development bank, financing small and mid-size business loans, housing and energy-efficiency programmes, student loans, export and project finance via KfW IPEX, and development aid through DEG. Headquartered in Frankfurt, owned 80 percent by the federal government and 20 percent by the states. It raises funds on capital markets with an explicit government guarantee. Total assets are around 600 billion euros or more. Well-known in Germany but public sector, with no commercial sponsorship tradition.

SoFi Technologies is a US digital financial services company offering student loan refinancing, personal loans, home loans, a checking and savings account, credit card, investing and crypto trading, plus the Galileo and Technisys platforms for other fintechs. It has over 12 million members and holds a national bank charter after buying Golden Pacific Bancorp in 2022. Headquartered in San Francisco, listed on Nasdaq (SOFI) via a 2021 SPAC merger. Strong consumer brand and naming-rights holder of SoFi Stadium in Los Angeles.

Bank of America is one of the largest US banks, offering consumer banking, credit and debit cards, mortgages, small business banking, wealth management through Merrill and Bank of America Private Bank, and corporate and investment banking through BofA Securities. It serves tens of millions of customers, with about 3,700 branches and total assets of over $3 trillion. Headquartered in Charlotte, North Carolina. Listed on NYSE (BAC). Very strong consumer brand, a long-time naming-rights holder and sponsor of sports, golf, soccer and the Chicago Marathon.

Bank of Shanghai is a mid-size Chinese commercial bank offering corporate and retail banking, wealth management, credit cards, and trade and financial markets services, headquartered in Shanghai (Crunchbase shows a Hong Kong address). Customers are Chinese consumers and businesses, especially in the Yangtze River Delta, with assets over CNY 3 trillion. Founded in 1995 and listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (601229). Local brand in China.

Banque Saudi Fransi (BSF) is a Saudi Arabian bank offering retail, corporate, treasury and investment banking, Islamic products, and brokerage through Alfransi Capital. Headquartered in Riyadh, it was established in 1977 as a joint venture, and French bank Credit Agricole has been a major shareholder. Customers are Saudi consumers and businesses, with assets of roughly 300 billion riyals. Listed on Tadawul (1050). Well-known banking brand in Saudi Arabia.

China Everbright Bank is a Chinese joint-stock commercial bank offering corporate and retail banking, credit cards, wealth management and financial markets services across China. Headquartered in Beijing, founded in 1992, with assets over CNY 6 trillion. Customers are Chinese consumers and businesses. State-linked shareholders include China Everbright Group and Central Huijin. Listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (601818) and Hong Kong (6818). Recognised Chinese bank brand.

China Minsheng Banking Corp is a Chinese joint-stock commercial bank founded in 1996 as the first bank mostly owned by private enterprises, offering corporate banking, retail banking, small business loans, credit cards and wealth management. Headquartered in Beijing, with assets over CNY 7 trillion. Customers are Chinese consumers and businesses. Listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (600016) and Hong Kong (1988). Recognised bank brand in China.

OneMain Financial is a leading US consumer lender, offering personal loans to nonprime customers through about 1,300 branches and online, along with credit cards and optional insurance products. Customers are middle-income Americans who may have limited access to bank credit, with revenue from interest and fees, and a loan book of about $24 billion. Crunchbase lists Baltimore, Maryland. Listed on NYSE (OMF). Established consumer finance brand in the US.

QNB Turkiye, formerly QNB Finansbank, is a Turkish bank headquartered in Istanbul, offering retail, SME, corporate and private banking, credit cards (CardFinans) and digital services through hundreds of branches. It is a subsidiary of Qatar National Bank (QNB Group), bought from National Bank of Greece in 2016. Listed on Borsa Istanbul (QNBTR). Recognised consumer bank in Turkey with active sports and cultural sponsorship.

Ualá is an Argentine fintech offering a digital bank account, a prepaid Mastercard, credit, investments and payments tools through its app, serving millions of users in Argentina, Mexico and Colombia. Founded in 2017 by Pierpaolo Barbieri and based in Buenos Aires. Revenue comes from card fees, lending and merchant services. Backed by investors including Soros Fund Management, SoftBank, Tencent and Ribbit Capital, and valued at about $2.75 billion in 2024. Private. Strong consumer brand in Argentina.

Navi is a Bengaluru-based financial services group founded by Flipkart co-founder Sachin Bansal, offering personal and home loans through Navi Finserv, a UPI payments app, mutual funds via Navi Mutual Fund, and general and health insurance through Navi General Insurance. Customers are Indian consumers using a mobile app. Has raised about $858 million. Private. Growing consumer fintech brand in India with national advertising. The brand name in the row contains an OCR error.

Neo Financial is a Calgary-based Canadian fintech offering the Neo Mastercard credit card with cash back, savings and high-interest accounts, mortgages and a payments business, with several million customers and partner merchants. Founded in 2019 by Andrew Chau and Jeff Adamson. Revenue comes from interchange, interest and partnerships. Has raised about $676 million in funding including debt. Private. Fast-growing Canadian consumer brand with visible partnerships.

Satispay is an Italian mobile payments app that lets users pay in shops and online and send money from their bank account without a card, accepted by hundreds of thousands of merchants in Italy and a few other European countries. Founded in 2013 and based in Milan. Revenue comes from merchant fees and services. Has raised about $567 million. Private, valued over 1 billion euros. Well-known consumer app in Italy.

Thought Machine is a London-based cloud-native core banking software company, selling its Vault Core platform to banks such as JPMorgan Chase, Lloyds, Standard Chartered and SEB. Founded in 2014 by former Google engineer Paul Taylor. Revenue comes from software licences and subscriptions. Has raised about $665 million in total funding and was valued around $2.7 billion in 2022. Private. B2B brand known in banking technology, with no consumer awareness.

Bank Hapoalim is Israel's largest bank by assets, offering retail, business, corporate and private banking, capital markets and credit cards through branches and digital channels, with operations abroad. Headquartered in Tel Aviv, founded in 1921. Customers are Israeli consumers and businesses. Listed on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (POLI). Very strong domestic brand, with sports sponsorship in Israel.

Bank Leumi is one of Israel's two largest banks, providing retail, business, private and corporate banking, mortgages, capital markets and its Pepper digital bank, with global operations. Headquartered in Tel Aviv, founded in 1902. Customers are Israeli consumers and businesses. Listed on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (LUMI). Strong domestic consumer brand.

EQT is a Stockholm-based global investment firm running private equity, infrastructure, real estate, growth and venture funds, with about 270 billion euros in assets under management and portfolio companies across Europe, North America and Asia. Customers are institutional investors such as pension funds and sovereign funds, with revenue from management fees and carried interest. Founded in 1994 with roots in the Wallenberg family's Investor AB. Listed on Nasdaq Stockholm (EQT) since 2019. Well-known in finance, low consumer awareness.

Eurobank is one of the four main Greek banks, offering retail, SME, corporate and private banking, plus insurance and asset management, with operations in Greece, Cyprus (it took control of Hellenic Bank in 2024), Bulgaria, Serbia and Luxembourg. Headquartered in Athens. Customers are consumers and businesses. Listed on the Athens Stock Exchange (EUROB). Strong consumer banking brand in Greece.

Global Payments is a merchant payments technology company headquartered in Atlanta, offering card acceptance, point-of-sale software, issuer processing and commerce tools to millions of businesses and financial institutions worldwide. It merged with TSYS in 2019 and, in 2025, agreed to buy Worldpay while selling its Issuer Solutions business to FIS. Revenue is about $10 billion. Listed on NYSE (GPN). B2B brand, known in banking and retail, with limited consumer awareness.

International Islamic Liquidity Management Corporation (IILM) is a Kuala Lumpur-based multilateral institution that issues short-term Shariah-compliant sukuk, giving Islamic financial institutions a tool to manage liquidity. It was established in 2010 and is owned by central banks and monetary authorities from countries including Malaysia, Kuwait, Turkey, Qatar and the UAE. Customers are Islamic banks and investors. Not listed. Institutional brand with no consumer awareness.

Kuwait Finance House (KFH) is one of the world's largest Islamic banks, offering Shariah-compliant retail, corporate, investment and real estate finance in Kuwait, Bahrain, Turkey, Malaysia, Saudi Arabia and elsewhere. Founded in 1977 and headquartered in Kuwait City, it merged with Ahli United Bank in 2022 and is a pioneer in Islamic banking. Listed on Boursa Kuwait (KFH). Strong consumer brand in Kuwait and the Gulf with significant advertising and sponsorship.

MuniFin (Municipality Finance Plc) is a Finnish credit institution that provides loans and leasing to municipalities, joint municipal authorities, and non-profit housing providers, funded by international bond issues with high credit ratings. Headquartered in Helsinki. Owned by Finnish municipalities, the pension provider Keva and the Finnish state. Revenue comes from interest margins. Not listed on an equity exchange. Public-sector finance brand with no consumer visibility.

Nordic Investment Bank (NIB) is a Helsinki-based international financial institution owned by Denmark, Estonia, Finland, Iceland, Latvia, Lithuania, Norway and Sweden, lending for projects that improve competitiveness and the environment, such as infrastructure, energy and innovation. It raises money in capital markets with a AAA rating. Customers are companies, public bodies and projects in member countries. Not listed. Institutional brand with no consumer visibility.

PKO Bank Polski (PKO BP) is Poland's largest bank, offering retail, SME, corporate and private banking, mortgages, cards, investment funds and insurance via its large branch network, the IKO mobile app and subsidiaries. Headquartered in Warsaw, founded in 1919 and controlled by the Polish state through the Treasury. Customers are about 11 million Polish clients. Listed on the Warsaw Stock Exchange (PKO). Very strong consumer brand in Poland with sports and cultural sponsorship.

Turk Eximbank is Turkey's state-owned export credit agency, giving export credits, guarantees and insurance to Turkish exporters, overseas investors and contractors, with financing for trade and projects abroad. Headquartered in Istanbul, owned by the Turkish Treasury. Customers are Turkish exporters and banks. Funding is raised from international bond markets and bank loans. Not listed. Public-sector finance brand with no consumer visibility.

Banco BPM is Italy's third-largest banking group by assets, offering retail, SME, corporate, private banking, bancassurance and asset management, with roots in northern Italy and a presence from Milan and Verona. Formed in 2017 from the merger of Banco Popolare and Banca Popolare di Milano. Credit Agricole is its largest shareholder. UniCredit made a takeover offer in 2024 and withdrew in 2025. Listed on Borsa Italiana (BAMI). Recognised consumer bank brand in northern Italy.

Banco Bradesco is one of Brazil's largest private banks, offering retail and corporate banking, credit cards, insurance (Bradesco Seguros), asset management and investment banking through more than 3,000 branches and a large digital customer base. Headquartered in Osasco, Sao Paulo, founded in 1943, with total assets of over one trillion reais. Listed on B3 (BBDC4) and NYSE (BBD). Very strong consumer brand in Brazil, with extensive sports and cultural sponsorships.

BBVA Mexico (formerly BBVA Bancomer) is Mexico's largest bank, offering retail, SME, corporate and investment banking, cards, mortgages, insurance and wealth management, with more than 25 million customers. Headquartered in Mexico City and nearly wholly owned by Spanish group BBVA. Its parent is listed on the Madrid stock exchange. Very strong consumer brand in Mexico, with major sports sponsorships including the Estadio BBVA naming in Monterrey and the long-running Liga BBVA MX title sponsorship.

BPER Banca is an Italian banking group based in Modena, providing retail, SME, corporate, private banking and bancassurance services through branches mainly in northern and central Italy. It expanded by acquiring Banca Popolare di Sondrio in 2025 after acquiring Intesa branches. Customers are Italian households and businesses. Listed on Borsa Italiana (BPE). Recognised regional consumer bank with local sports and cultural sponsorships.

Bread Financial, formerly Alliance Data Systems, is a Columbus, Ohio financial services company offering private-label and co-brand credit cards, buy now pay later, and savings products, working with retail partners such as Ulta Beauty, Wayfair and Signet. Revenue comes from interest and fees on card balances. Listed on NYSE (BFH). B2B2C brand: known in retail partnerships, with the Bread name less known to consumers.

BTG Pactual is Latin America's largest independent investment bank, offering investment banking, asset management, wealth management, trading, research and a retail digital bank, with operations across Brazil, Latin America, the US and Europe. Headquartered in Sao Paulo, founded in 1983, and led by Andre Esteves. Customers are institutions, wealthy individuals and mass-market digital users. Listed on B3 (BPAC11). Strong finance brand in Brazil, with sports sponsorship.

Columbia Financial is the holding company for Columbia Bank in New Jersey, a community bank offering consumer and commercial banking, mortgages and business loans through more than 60 branches in New Jersey and New York, with assets of roughly $10 billion. Headquartered in Fair Lawn, New Jersey. Listed on Nasdaq (CLBK), with Columbia Bank MHC as majority owner. Regional consumer bank, no national awareness.

Commercial Bank of Qatar (CBQ) is a Doha-based Qatari bank offering conventional retail, corporate and private banking, cards, treasury and investment services, and owns Alternatif Bank in Turkey and has a stake in United Arab Bank of the UAE. Founded in 1975. Customers are Qatari consumers and companies. Listed on the Qatar Stock Exchange (CBQK). Recognisable consumer bank in Qatar with sports and event sponsorship.

Ellington Financial is a specialty finance company that acquires and manages residential mortgage loans, mortgage-backed securities, consumer loans and other credit assets, externally managed by Ellington Management Group. Headquartered in Old Greenwich, Connecticut, and structured as a real estate investment trust. Revenue comes from net interest income and investment gains. Listed on NYSE (EFC). Investor-focused brand with no consumer awareness.

Encore Capital Group is an international specialty finance company that buys and collects defaulted consumer debt, including credit card receivables, through Midland Credit Management in the US and Cabot Credit Management in the UK. Headquartered in San Diego, California. Revenue comes from collections on purchased portfolios, at around $1.5 billion. Listed on Nasdaq (ECPG). Debt-collection brand with limited public recognition and reputational sensitivity.

Equitable Bank, the main subsidiary of EQB Inc., is a Toronto-based Canadian Schedule I bank focused on residential mortgages, commercial lending and its digital EQ Bank, which offers high-interest savings, term deposits and no-fee accounts. Founded in 1970. Customers are Canadian consumers, mortgage borrowers and businesses, with about C$130 billion in assets. Listed on the TSX (EQB). Digital banking brand known to Canadian savers.

Guotai Junan Securities was a major Chinese brokerage and investment bank offering securities trading, wealth management, investment banking, asset management and research, with a large retail customer base in China. Headquartered in Shanghai. In 2025 it merged with Haitong Securities to form Guotai Haitong Securities. Listed on the Shanghai and Hong Kong exchanges. Well-known financial brand in China, with little overseas consumer awareness.

IDFC FIRST Bank is an Indian private-sector bank formed in 2018 by the merger of IDFC Bank and Capital First, offering retail banking, credit cards, vehicle and home loans, microfinance and corporate banking to millions of customers through branches and digital channels. Headquartered in Mumbai. Listed on the NSE and BSE (IDFCFIRSTB). Recognised consumer bank in India with active marketing.

IIFL Finance is a Mumbai-based Indian non-banking finance company offering gold loans, home loans, business loans and microfinance, through about 4,000 branches across India. Customers are retail borrowers and small businesses, with revenue from interest. It spun off from the IIFL group in 2019 and, in 2024, faced a temporary regulatory restriction on gold loans. Listed on the NSE and BSE (IIFL). Recognised consumer finance brand in India.

Kiavi, formerly LendingHome, is a tech-enabled lender providing short-term fix and flip loans and rental loans to residential real estate investors across the US, using an online platform for underwriting. Revenue comes from interest and fees. Headquartered in San Francisco, though Crunchbase lists Pittsburgh. Crunchbase shows about $1.85 billion in funding, mostly debt facilities. Private. B2B brand known among real estate investors.

National Bank of Canada is Canada's sixth-largest bank, offering personal and commercial banking, wealth management, and capital markets, with a strong base in Quebec and a financial markets business that includes Credigy in the US and ABA Bank in Cambodia. Headquartered in Montreal, founded in 1859. Listed on the TSX (NA). Strong consumer brand in Quebec and sponsor of the National Bank Open tennis tournament.

NatWest Group is a major UK banking group, owning NatWest, Royal Bank of Scotland and Coutts, serving retail, business and private banking customers across Great Britain. Headquartered in Edinburgh, with London operations. The UK government became the largest shareholder after the 2008 bailout and has since sold down its stake. Listed on the London Stock Exchange (NWG) and NYSE. Very strong UK consumer brand, with a record of major sports sponsorships.

The New Development Bank (NDB) is a multilateral development bank founded by the BRICS countries (Brazil, Russia, India, China and South Africa) in 2014 and headquartered in Shanghai, financing infrastructure and sustainable development projects in emerging economies, with new members including Bangladesh, the UAE and Egypt. Its president is Dilma Rousseff. Funded by member capital and bond issuance. Not listed. Institutional brand with no consumer visibility.

NRW.BANK is the development bank of the German state of North Rhine-Westphalia, based in Dusseldorf and Munster, providing promotional loans for housing, businesses, startups, municipalities and infrastructure, and funding itself with state-guaranteed bonds. Owned by the state of North Rhine-Westphalia and the regional association Landschaftsverband. Customers are businesses, municipalities and housing investors. Not listed. Public-sector finance brand with regional recognition in Germany.

Saudi bank formed in 2019 when Saudi British Bank (SABB) merged with Alawwal Bank, headquartered in Riyadh and part-owned by HSBC. Provides retail, corporate, treasury and investment banking, with several hundred branches in Saudi Arabia and one of the country's larger loan books. Listed on Tadawul (1060). Established consumer banking brand in the Kingdom with limited international profile, relevant for Saudi-linked activations.

Externally managed business development company that lends to middle-market US companies, managed by Sixth Street, the global investment firm. Earns interest income from senior secured loans, paying dividends to public shareholders. Listed on the NYSE (TSLX). Pure financial vehicle, B2B only, with essentially no consumer visibility or sponsorship profile. It has a portfolio of loans worth over $3 billion, and shareholders earn dividends from interest income.

London-headquartered international bank, founded 1853, serving Asia, Africa and the Middle East with wealth, corporate and institutional banking. Operates in around 50 markets with about 85,000 staff. Listed in London and Hong Kong (STAN). Strong brand in Asia and a history of sponsorship, including Liverpool and Formula 1 team deals in the past. It has about 1,000 branches and a strong presence in Singapore, Hong Kong, India, the UAE and Africa.

loc: Rio De Janeiro, Rio de Jan...
about: Brazil's federal development bank, BNDES, headquartered in Rio de Janeiro and wholly state-owned, financing infrastructure, industry, exports and innovation across the country with long-term loans. Customers are companies, states and municipalities. Among the largest development banks in the world by loan book. Institutional brand with limited consumer awareness. BNDES is among the largest development banks in the world, with loans comparable to the World Bank group.

Wilmington-based online personal lending platform, Best Egg, offering personal loans and credit cards to US consumers. Owned by Marlette Holdings. Funding of about $1.5 billion shown. Consumer finance brand with moderate awareness. Offers loans of up to $50,000 through an online platform, and many borrowers refinance credit cards. Revenue is interest and fees. Moderate US consumer awareness. Best Egg also offers credit card products, and the company says it has served millions of customers since its founding in 2014.

Ho Chi Minh City-based Vietnamese bank, HDBank, founded 1990, offering retail, SME and corporate banking, with ties to HD Group and Vietjet. Listed on HOSE (HDB). Strong consumer brand in Vietnam, with sponsorship in sports and aviation. Has over 300 branches and millions of customers. Strong consumer brand in Vietnam and connected to the airline Vietjet. HDBank is controlled by Sovico Group, and it provides retail loans, cards and wealth products, with a strong presence in southern Vietnam.

Enova International is a US online lending and fintech company that provides short-term credit, installment loans, lines of credit and small business financing under brands such as CashNet, NetCredit, OnDeck and Headway Capital. Customers are non-prime consumers and small businesses, and it uses proprietary analytics for underwriting. Founded in 2004 as part of Cash America, spun out in 2014; headquartered in Chicago and listed on the NYSE (ENVA). Reports around 3 billion dollars of annual revenue, largely in the United States and Brazil. Moderate brand awareness among consumers who borrow.

Chongqing Ant Consumer Finance (Ant Consumer Finance) is a licensed Chinese consumer finance company established in Chongqing in 2020, majority controlled by Ant Group and Chongqing financial interests, offering consumer loans through Alipay platforms such as Huabei (Ant Credit Pay) and Jiebei. It lends to individuals in China and had registered capital of around 8 billion yuan, with funding shown at 6 billion yuan. Strong brand exposure through the Ant and Alipay ecosystem within China only, and under strict financial regulation.
cb_desc: Chongqing Ant Consumer Finance operates as a consum....

about: Qifu Technology (formerly 360 DigiTech) is a Chinese credit-tech platform operating the 360 Jietiao app, which connects consumers and small business owners with banks and licensed financial institutions through loan facilitation, risk-management services and insurance. It was spun from Qihoo 360 and is based in Shanghai, listed on Nasdaq (QFIN) since 2018. Revenue is several billion yuan per year. Strong brand exposure to Chinese borrowers, but limited presence outside China, and sector subject to heavy regulation.

Zilch is a UK fintech offering interest-free buy-now-pay-later at checkout and a virtual Mastercard, funded in part by advertising and by merchant fees rather than consumer interest. Founded in 2018, it is headquartered in London, with customers across the UK and Europe and a licence in the US. It has raised funding from Goldman Sachs and other investors and reached a valuation of more than 2 billion dollars. Known to UK consumers through its high-profile marketing and sponsorships, including football and sports partnerships.

PayJoy is a San Francisco fintech that finances smartphone purchases for people with limited credit history in emerging markets, using a lock-and-unlock technology that restricts the phone if payments stop. It operates in Mexico, Brazil, India, South Africa, Indonesia, Colombia and the US, working with retail partners, and has financed millions of phones. Founded in 2015, it has raised several hundred million dollars in equity and debt from Andreessen Horowitz, Valar and others. Little consumer brand recognition outside the sales channel.

Stash is a US consumer fintech app that offers investing, banking, retirement accounts and financial education, targeting beginners, with fractional shares and auto-investing from small amounts. It has several million customers and revenue from monthly subscriptions. Headquartered in New York, founded in 2015, it has raised nearly 700 million dollars from investors including Union Square Ventures, Goodwater Capital and Coatue. Known to US consumers through national advertising and partnerships but still a niche brand.

Africa Finance Corporation is a multilateral development finance institution founded in 2007 by African governments and headquartered in Lagos, investing in infrastructure projects across the continent in power, transport, telecoms, heavy industry and natural resources. Member states include Nigeria and many others; it has an investment-grade rating and balance sheet of over 10 billion dollars. B2B and government-focused with little consumer brand awareness; sponsorship fit is limited to institutional visibility.

BNG Bank (Bank Nederlandse Gemeenten) is the Dutch bank of local authorities, based in The Hague, providing loans and financing to Dutch municipalities, housing associations, healthcare institutions and public bodies. It is owned by the Dutch state and municipalities and is one of the Netherlands' largest banks by balance sheet. Funding is raised on international capital markets. B2B and public sector with no consumer brand profile.

about: The African Development Bank is a multilateral development finance institution founded in 1964, headquartered in Abidjan, Cote d'Ivoire, owned by African and non-African member states. It lends to governments and private companies for infrastructure, agriculture, energy and climate projects across Africa, and holds the highest credit ratings. Customers are governments and corporates. Government institution with no consumer brand; sponsorship fit limited to development or Africa-focused visibility.

Afreximbank, the African Export-Import Bank, is a pan-African multilateral financial institution headquartered in Cairo, founded in 1993, offering trade finance, guarantees and project funding to African governments, banks and exporters. It has a high investment-grade-like profile, runs the Intra-African Trade Fair and has shareholders including African central banks. B2B institution with a high profile in African finance circles; it has done sports sponsorship in Africa.

ANZ (Australia and New Zealand Banking Group) is one of Australia's big four banks, headquartered in Melbourne, providing retail, business and institutional banking in Australia, New Zealand and across Asia and the Pacific. It has about 40,000 staff and serves around 8 million customers, and is listed on the ASX (ANZ). Total assets exceed one trillion Australian dollars. Very high consumer visibility in Australia and New Zealand, and a major sports sponsor including rugby, cricket and the Australian Open.

Bank of Industry is a Nigerian development finance institution headquartered in Lagos, owned by the federal government, the Central Bank of Nigeria and the Ministry of Finance Incorporated, and provides long-term loans to manufacturing, agro-processing, mining and small businesses. It is Nigeria's oldest and largest development bank, founded in 1964 as the Nigerian Industrial Development Bank. Government-linked with strong name recognition among Nigerian businesses and little outside Nigeria.

Bank of Ireland is one of Ireland's biggest retail and commercial banks, headquartered in Dublin, providing current accounts, mortgages, business lending, life insurance and wealth services through branches and digital channels. It is listed on Euronext Dublin and the London Stock Exchange (BIRG) and founded in 1783. Customers are Irish households and businesses. Very high consumer visibility in Ireland, including sponsorship of rugby and Gaelic games.

BDO Unibank is the largest bank in the Philippines by assets, headquartered in Makati, a member of the SM Group of Henry Sy's family, with about 1,600 branches and a broad consumer, corporate and investment banking offering. Listed on the Philippine Stock Exchange (BDO). Customers are Filipino households and companies, and overseas Filipino workers. Very high consumer visibility in the Philippines and a prominent sports sponsor, with limited overseas awareness.

The Central American Bank for Economic Integration (CABEI) is a multilateral development bank based in Tegucigalpa, Honduras, owned by Central American governments and other member countries, lending to governments and private companies for infrastructure, energy, education and economic integration. Founded in 1960. B2B and government-focused, with no consumer brand awareness.

Ecobank (Ecobank Transnational Incorporated) is a pan-African banking group present in about 35 African countries, offering retail, commercial and corporate banking and payments. Holding company based in Lome, Togo, and listed on the Nigerian, Ghanaian and West African exchanges. It has been a prominent sponsor of African football and sport. Strong consumer brand in West and Central Africa, with revenue in the billions of dollars.

Hartree Partners is a New York merchant commodities firm trading and investing in physical energy, power, natural gas, metals and renewables, and also structuring financing. It serves producers, utilities and industrial customers worldwide. The business has been backed by Oaktree Capital Management, the investment firm. B2B commodity merchant with no consumer brand awareness.
cb_desc: Hartree Partners is a merchant commodities firm specializing...

about: KeyBank is the principal subsidiary of KeyCorp, a US regional bank holding company based in Cleveland, Ohio, offering retail, commercial and investment banking across about 15 states with roughly 1,000 branches. KeyCorp is listed on the NYSE (KEY) and has total assets around 190 billion dollars. Customers include consumers, small and mid-sized businesses and corporate clients. Well known across the Midwest and Northeast US.

Mizrahi Tefahot Bank is Israel's third-largest bank by assets, headquartered in Tel Aviv, specialising in mortgages and retail banking and serving households, businesses and institutions. It is listed on the Tel Aviv Stock Exchange (MZTF) and controlled by the Ofer family and other holders. Founded in 2004 through the merger of Mizrahi Bank and Tefahot. High consumer visibility in Israel, with a focus on housing finance and minimal overseas presence.

Ping An Insurance is a Chinese financial conglomerate headquartered in Shenzhen, offering life and property insurance, banking (Ping An Bank), asset management and fintech such as Lufax and OneConnect. Founded in 1988, it has more than 200 million retail customers, is listed in Hong Kong (2318) and Shanghai (601318), and has revenue of over one trillion yuan. Very high consumer visibility in China, and it has been a major sports sponsor in China, including football.

Scalapay is an Italian buy-now-pay-later fintech, founded in 2019 by Simone Mancini and Johnny Mitrevski, which lets shoppers split purchases into three or four interest-free instalments at online and in-store merchants in Italy, Spain, Germany, France and elsewhere. Merchants pay fees, and the Crunchbase HQ is shown as Dublin, with main operations in Milan. It has raised hundreds of millions of dollars in equity and debt. Known to Italian online shoppers, with some sports marketing.

The State Bank of Pakistan is the country's central bank, headquartered in Karachi and established in 1948, responsible for monetary policy, banking regulation, foreign exchange reserves and currency issue. It is government-owned and not a commercial seller of products. No consumer brand in the usual sense, so it is not a likely sponsor.

SumUp is a London-based fintech that provides card readers, point-of-sale systems, online payments, invoicing and business accounts for small merchants, operating in more than 30 markets across Europe, the Americas and beyond. Founded in 2012 in Germany, it has served millions of merchants and raised billions of dollars in equity and debt, with a valuation of over 8 billion euros in 2022. Strong B2B brand among small businesses, backed by heavy advertising, and a sponsor of sports properties.

VPBank (Vietnam Prosperity Joint Stock Commercial Bank) is one of Vietnam's largest private banks, based in Hanoi, providing retail, SME and corporate banking, credit cards, consumer finance via FE Credit, and insurance. Sumitomo Mitsui Banking Corporation bought a minority stake in 2023. Listed on the Ho Chi Minh Stock Exchange (VPB). Very visible among Vietnamese consumers with heavy marketing, including sports sponsorship.

Aareal Bank is a German property financing and software bank, headquartered in Wiesbaden, providing commercial property loans and digital payments and software for the housing industry. Advent International and Centerbridge took it private in 2023. It was formerly listed on the Frankfurt Stock Exchange. B2B bank with little consumer brand awareness.

Bank of Beijing is a Chinese commercial bank, listed on the Shanghai Stock Exchange (601169), serving corporate, retail and small business customers primarily in Beijing and other cities. ING and International Finance Corporation were early shareholders. It is one of the major city commercial banks with assets over 3 trillion yuan. Strong local brand in Beijing, with little overseas visibility.

Chime is a San Francisco financial technology company offering mobile-first banking accounts with no monthly fees, via partner banks, with early wage access (MyPay), a Credit Builder card and Spot Me overdraft protection. It serves about 9 million active US members, mostly lower to middle-income consumers, and listed on Nasdaq (CHYM) in June 2025. Revenue is over 2 billion dollars, mostly from interchange fees. Founded in 2012. Strong US consumer brand with heavy advertising and sports sponsorships.

Citizens Bank is a US regional bank headquartered in Providence, Rhode Island, and part of Citizens Financial Group (NYSE: CFG), with about 1,000 branches in 14 states across New England, the Mid-Atlantic and the Midwest, serving retail, small business and corporate clients. Customers include consumers and mid-sized companies. Total assets are around 220 billion dollars. Formerly owned by Royal Bank of Scotland until its 2015 IPO. Strong regional brand recognition and a sponsor of sports venues in Boston.

eCapital is a Miami, Florida, commercial finance firm that provides factoring, asset-based lending and equipment finance to small and mid-sized businesses in North America, Europe and Latin America, and has grown through acquiring other factoring firms. It is backed by private equity. Funding shown is about 1.8 billion dollars, likely including debt facilities. B2B lender with little consumer brand awareness.

about: IndusInd Bank is an Indian private-sector bank headquartered in Mumbai (Crunchbase shows Pune), founded in 1994 by the Hinduja group, offering retail, corporate and microfinance banking, vehicle finance and credit cards across about 3,000 branches. Listed on the NSE and BSE (INDUSINDBK), with assets over 4 trillion rupees. The bank faced derivatives accounting issues in 2025. Well known in India as a retail brand and a sponsor of cricket and Formula 1-related events.

IntraFi is a US financial technology company in Arlington, Virginia, that runs a network letting banks place customers' large deposits across many institutions so they qualify for full FDIC insurance, through its ICS and CDARS services. Customers are banks, credit unions, businesses and municipalities. Formerly Promontory Interfinancial Network, it is privately held. B2B financial infrastructure with no consumer brand awareness.

MidCap Financial Investment Corporation, formerly Apollo Investment Corporation, is a US business development company managed by an Apollo Global Management affiliate, which lends to middle-market companies, mostly senior secured loans. Listed on Nasdaq (MFIC), it earns interest income. Crunchbase shows a Michigan location, which looks like an error. B2B financial vehicle with no consumer brand awareness.

about: PennyMac refers to PennyMac Financial Services, a US mortgage lender and servicer based in Westlake Village, California (NYSE: PFSI), one of the largest mortgage servicers and a top originator of home loans, sold directly to consumers and through wholesale brokers and correspondent lenders. It is linked to the PennyMac Mortgage Investment Trust (PMT). Customers are US home buyers and refinancers. Revenue is over 3 billion dollars. Strong brand awareness in US mortgage markets with sports advertising.

Sammaan Capital, formerly Indiabulls Housing Finance, is an Indian non-banking housing finance company based in Mumbai, offering home loans, loans against property and construction finance mainly in the affordable housing segment. Renamed in 2024 after a change in controlling ownership, with Abu Dhabi's International Holding Company (IHC) acquiring a stake in 2025. Listed on the NSE and BSE. Customers are individuals and developers across India. Moderate brand recognition in Indian lending.

Bangkok Bank is Thailand's largest bank by assets, founded in 1944 and headquartered in Bangkok, with a large international network in Asia, offering retail, SME and corporate banking, trade finance and cross-border QR payments. Listed on the Stock Exchange of Thailand (BBL), it is controlled by the Sophonpanich family. Strong consumer brand in Thailand and across Southeast Asia, including a history of sponsorship in sport and events.

Current is a New York mobile banking platform offering checking accounts through partner banks, early direct deposit, savings pods and credit-building tools, mainly for younger and lower-income customers. Founded in 2015, it has raised about 680 million dollars and claims millions of members. Revenue comes from interchange fees and subscriptions. Known to US neobank users, with limited broader awareness.

Allica Bank is a UK digital bank for established small and medium-sized businesses, founded in 2018 and based in London, offering business current accounts, savings, commercial mortgages and asset finance, with a banking licence granted in 2019. It reached unicorn status after raising funding of over 500 million dollars. Customers are UK SMEs, and the brand is known in the UK business banking community with marketing aimed at business owners.

Slice is an Indian fintech, formerly a credit card and consumer lending start-up, headquartered in Bengaluru, that offered small loans and a payment card. It merged with North East Small Finance Bank in 2024, becoming a digital-first small finance bank known as slice Small Finance Bank, regulated by the Reserve Bank of India. Customers are young Indian consumers. Strong awareness among young app users, with active marketing.

Yamaha Motor Finance Corporation, USA is the finance arm of Yamaha Motor in the US, based in Cypress, California, providing retail loans, floor plan financing and extended service contracts for customers and dealers of Yamaha motorcycles, ATVs, marine products and golf cars. It is a subsidiary of Yamaha Motor Co. (Japan) and part of the Yamaha Motor Corporation USA. Strong brand association with Yamaha, with a company well known for motorsport.
